key_insight: HVD mimics human visual attention with a coarse-to-fine alignment so text-video retrieval models focus on salient frames and regions rather than being 'blinded' by background noise, improving cross-modal matching accuracy.
problem_solved: Current text-video retrieval models perform 'blind' feature interaction: sparse textual queries make it hard to identify and align the few key visual cues in noisy, long videos, producing weak or ambiguous matches.
method: Coarse frame-level relevance: estimate and select a small set of candidate frames that are most likely relevant to the text query, reducing temporal noise.
Fine-grained region-level alignment: within selected frames, apply human-vision-inspired saliency/attention to prioritize salient patches/objects for precise text-region matching.
Integration with CLIP-style encoders and contrastive/cross-modal training to learn aligned video and text representations while keeping computations focused on informative content.
impact: By directing attention to human-relevant visual cues, HVD yields more accurate, robust, and interpretable text-video retrieval while reducing unnecessary computation—useful for practitioners building scalable multimodal search and retrieval systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: coarse-to-fine flow from full video -> selected frames -> salient regions -> text alignment

Bar/line chart: retrieval metric improvements (e.g., Recall@K) comparing baseline CLIP-style method vs HVD
Icon set: CLIP encoder, attention/saliency spotlight, contrastive loss, and speed/efficiency gauge
paper_title: HVD: Human Vision-Driven Video Representation Learning for Text-Video Retrieval
paper_authors: Zequn Xie, Xin Liu, Boyun Zhang, Yuxiao Lin, Sihang Cai
